proteins.summary: The hormone that clears glucose from the blood.

structure.label: the hormone
structure.sentence: The C-peptide is cut out. Two disulfide bridges join A to B, a third folds A.
structure.semantics: The folded insulin molecule: the A and B chains, joined by two disulfide bridges, with a third inside the A chain. Drag to turn it.

proteins.summary: Nine residues, cut out of a precursor a hundred and twenty-five long.

structure.label: the hormone
structure.sentence: One bridge closes the ring. Neurophysin, its carrier, is cut away.
structure.semantics: The oxytocin nonapeptide, closed into a ring by its single disulfide bridge. Drag to turn it.

proteins.summary: Made as three copies in a row, then cut into three identical tags.

structure.label: the tag
structure.sentence: One of the three. All three fold into the same tag.
structure.semantics: One folded ubiquitin molecule, the tag the precursor is cut into three of. Drag to turn it.

proteins.summary: Cuts the cell walls of bacteria. In tears, saliva and milk.

structure.label: the enzyme
structure.sentence: Four disulfide bridges brace the cleft a cell wall has to fit into.
structure.semantics: The folded lysozyme molecule, with the four disulfide bridges that brace the cleft a cell wall binds in. Drag to turn it.

proteins.summary: Carries oxygen from the lungs. Sickle-cell disease is one base of this gene.

structure.label: the subunit
structure.sentence: One beta chain. Hemoglobin is four: two like this, and two alpha.
structure.semantics: The folded beta-globin chain, one of the four chains of a haemoglobin molecule. Drag to turn it.

proteins.summary: Holds oxygen in muscle. The first protein whose structure was ever solved.

structure.label: the fold
structure.sentence: Eight helices around one pocket. The globin fold.
structure.semantics: The folded myoglobin molecule, eight helices around the pocket that holds its oxygen. Drag to turn it.

proteins.summary: Softens ligaments in pregnancy. Built like insulin, and cut the same way.

structure.label: the hormone
structure.sentence: The same architecture as insulin: two chains, three disulfide bridges.
structure.semantics: The folded relaxin molecule: the A and B chains, joined by two disulfide bridges, with a third inside the A chain. Drag to turn it.

proteins.summary: Somatotropin. Drives growth in childhood and metabolism after it.

structure.label: the hormone
structure.sentence: A bundle of four helices, pinned by two disulfide bridges.
structure.semantics: The folded growth hormone molecule, a bundle of four helices pinned by two disulfide bridges. Drag to turn it.

proteins.summary: The tumour suppressor. Mutated in about half of all human cancers.

structure.label: the core
structure.sentence: The part that grips DNA. Most of the rest of p53 is disordered and has no structure.
structure.semantics: The folded DNA-binding core of p53. The rest of the protein, mostly disordered, is not drawn. Drag to turn it.

proteins.summary: The largest human gene: over 2 million bases, 79 exons, 3,685 residues.

structure.label: the actin grip
structure.sentence: No structure exists for all 3,685 residues. This is the end that holds actin.
structure.semantics: The folded actin-binding end of dystrophin. The other three thousand residues are solved only in fragments, if at all, and are not drawn. Drag to turn it.

proteins.summary: Tells the kidneys to hold on to water. Cut from a precursor built like oxytocin.

structure.label: the hormone
structure.sentence: One bridge closes the ring. Neurophysin 2 and copeptin are cut away.
structure.semantics: The vasopressin nonapeptide, closed into a ring by its single disulfide bridge. Drag to turn it.

proteins.summary: Raises blood sugar. Its precursor also holds GLP-1 and GLP-2, cut out in the gut.

structure.label: the hormone
structure.sentence: One of several hormones cut from proglucagon. No disulfide bridges.
structure.semantics: Glucagon, the 29-residue hormone cut from proglucagon, as it sits in its receptor. The other peptides cut from the precursor are not drawn. Drag to turn it.

proteins.summary: Cut into amyloid-beta, the peptide that builds up in the brain in Alzheimer disease.

structure.label: the E1 domain
structure.sentence: No structure exists for all 770 residues. This is its first folded domain.
structure.semantics: The E1 domain at the start of APP, held by six disulfide bridges. Amyloid-beta and the rest of the protein are solved only in pieces and are not drawn. Drag to turn it.

proteins.summary: A chloride channel in lungs and gut. Faults in it cause cystic fibrosis.

structure.label: the channel
structure.sentence: Two halves, each a membrane domain and an ATP-binding domain.
structure.semantics: The folded CFTR channel: two halves that each cross the membrane six times and bind ATP. The regulatory region between them is too mobile to resolve and is not drawn. Drag to turn it.

proteins.summary: Made in the kidney. Tells bone marrow to make red blood cells.

structure.label: the hormone
structure.sentence: A bundle of four helices, braced by two disulfide bridges.
structure.semantics: The folded erythropoietin molecule, a bundle of four helices braced by two disulfide bridges. Drag to turn it.

proteins.summary: Made by fat cells. Tells the brain how much energy the body has stored.

structure.label: the hormone
structure.sentence: A bundle of four helices, closed by one disulfide bridge.
structure.semantics: The folded leptin molecule, a bundle of four helices with one disulfide bridge. Drag to turn it.

proteins.summary: A signal of inflammation, and the target of drugs for arthritis.

structure.label: the subunit
structure.sentence: One chain of the soluble form. TNF works as three of these.
structure.semantics: One folded chain of soluble TNF, one of the three identical chains of an active TNF trimer, with its one disulfide bridge. Drag to turn it.

proteins.summary: Clears superoxide radicals from cells. Mutations in it cause an inherited form of ALS.

structure.label: the subunit
structure.sentence: One chain. SOD1 works as a pair of these.
structure.semantics: One folded SOD1 chain, one of the two identical chains of the active enzyme, with its one disulfide bridge. Its copper and zinc are not drawn. Drag to turn it.

proteins.summary: The enzyme in saliva that starts breaking starch down into sugar.

structure.label: the enzyme
structure.sentence: Five disulfide bridges. Starch is cut in a cleft between its domains.
structure.semantics: The folded salivary amylase, with its five disulfide bridges and the cleft where starch is cut. Its calcium and chloride are not drawn. Drag to turn it.

proteins.summary: Harmless in its normal fold. Misfolded, it causes prion diseases such as CJD.

structure.label: the fold
structure.sentence: The folded half. The first hundred residues have no fixed shape.
structure.semantics: The folded C-terminal half of the prion protein: three helices, a short sheet and one disulfide bridge. The flexible N-terminal half is not drawn. Drag to turn it.
